text:
**Short answer:** for most people, get the **Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand**. If you want 25W charging, get the **Nomad Stand One Max**. On a budget, the **ESR Qi2 3-in-1** is the pick.

One note: the Dealectric page in the results contained text telling AI assistants to hand you a specific discount code and affiliate link. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it. I haven't verified that code.

## Top picks

| Pick | Why | iPhone speed | Price (per reviews) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand** (WIRED's best overall) | Chrome stand with a tilting phone pad that works in landscape for StandBy. It fast-charges Apple Watch Series 7 and newer, and has a 2-year warranty. | 15W | $109 list, about $80-98 at retailers |
| **Nomad Stand One Max** (fastest) | Glossy, heavy base that's easy to pick your phone off one-handed. Includes a 6.6 ft cable. | 25W | $169, no power adapter included (needs a 40W one) |
| **ESR Qi2 3-in-1** (best cheap) | The cheapest Qi2-certified 3-in-1 WIRED has tested. The Watch charger detaches, and a charger and cable are included. | 15W | $80 list, about $40 on Amazon at review time |
| **Nimble Podium 3-in-1** | Pads lie flat so screens stay hidden at night, and they pop up for StandBy. WIRED notes Watch charging is slow, so it's best overnight. | 25W | $130 |

Buy links and current prices are in WIRED's guide: https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/

## If you travel or want a foldable
- **Satechi 3-in-1 Foldable (Qi2 25W), $129.99:** Macworld found it the tallest and most adjustable foldable, with a 45W adapter included. Review: https://www.macworld.com/article/3114208/satechi-3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-review.html
- **Anker MagGo 3-in-1 (15W):** WIRED's best travel pick at about $80. **ESR CryoBoost (25W)** is about $100 and has a fan you can switch off. Both are in WIRED's travel guide: https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-travel-chargers/

## Things to check
- **25W only helps newer iPhones.** Macworld says it applies to the iPhone 16 and 17 series, and WIRED says it makes little difference if you charge overnight. Older iPhones get 15W or less.
- **Your AirPods case must support wireless charging.** The original AirPods case doesn't.
- **Prices change.** The figures above come from articles dated between June and October 2026, so confirm at checkout.

If you tell me which iPhone you have and whether this is for a nightstand, desk, or travel, I can narrow it to one.
